summary: The game crashes when putting items with max stack sizes above 64 into bundles
description: The Bug: The game crashes when putting items with max stack sizes above 64 into bundles. A crash report regarding this has been attached and can be found below. Stack Trace: [^crash-2024-03-20_16.42.33-client.txt] Description: Container click java.lang.ArithmeticException: / by zero at cvk$a.c(SourceFile:134) at cvk$a.a(SourceFile:145) at crg.a(SourceFile:90) at csz.a(SourceFile:461) at cod.a(SourceFile:535) at cod.b(SourceFile:408) at cod.a(SourceFile:294) at fmq.a(SourceFile:370) at fmb.b(SourceFile:521) at fmq.b(SourceFile:606) at fdf.a(SourceFile:103) at fld.a(SourceFile:453) at fdf.a(SourceFile:103) at fdf.c(SourceFile:186) at boc.execute(SourceFile:108) at fdf.b(SourceFile:186) at org.lwjgl.glfw.GLFWMouseButtonCallbackI.callback(GLFWMouseButtonCallbackI.java:43) at org.lwjgl.system.JNI.invokeV(Native Method) at org.lwjgl.glfw.GLFW.glfwWaitEventsTimeout(GLFW.java:3509) at com.mojang.blaze3d.systems.RenderSystem.limitDisplayFPS(SourceFile:236) at fde.c(SourceFile:1364) at fde.f(SourceFile:895) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:265) Steps to Reproduce: - Obtain a bundle. - Give yourself a diamond sword with a max stack size of 65 by using the command provided below. /give @s minecraft:diamond_sword[minecraft:max_stack_size=65] 1 - Put the diamond sword into the bundle. Observed Behavior: The game crashes. Expected Behavior: The game would not crash.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Obtain a bundle.
3. Use the command to give yourself a diamond sword with a max stack size of 65:  
   `/give @s minecraft:diamond_sword[minecraft:max_stack_size=65] 1`
4. Put the diamond sword into the bundle.
5. Observe that the game crashes.
Observed Behavior:
When attempting to place items with a maximum stack size greater than 64, such as a diamond sword with a stack size of 65, into a bundle, the game crashes unexpectedly. This crash occurs due to an `ArithmeticException` caused by a division by zero error in the game's code, as indicated in the stack trace provided. Specifically, the crash report highlights that the issue arises during the container click event, which is triggered when the player interacts with the bundle interface. 

This behavior is not consistent with the expected functionality of bundles, which are designed to hold multiple items regardless of their stack sizes, as long as the total number of items does not exceed the bundle's capacity. Instead of successfully placing the item into the bundle, the game terminates, leading to a frustrating experience for players who attempt to manage their inventory using this feature. 

The crash can be reproduced consistently by following the steps outlined in the report, confirming that this is a critical issue that needs to be addressed to ensure the stability of item management within the game.
Expected Behavior: When attempting to place items with maximum stack sizes above 64 into bundles, the game should allow the action to occur without any crashes, enabling players to manage their inventory effectively. The bundle should accept the item, and players should be able to see the item inside the bundle, maintaining the expected functionality of item storage in Minecraft.
